key_insight: Spin SYK-dot chains separate entanglement within dots from entanglement across links, making dot size and link strength key controls on simulation difficulty.
engineering_relevance: Estimated ground-state quantum advantage requires roughly 15–21 qubits per dot or more and two-qubit error rates around 10⁻⁶ for even one Trotter step, beyond NISQ capabilities.
method: Connect dense p-qubit spin SYK dots with single ZZ links of strength K.
Bound entanglement across cuts and estimate quantum simulation resources.
Test estimates using blockwise imaginary-time MPS, exact diagonalisation, and noisy variational circuits.
evidence_signal: MPS matched exact diagonalisation at (p, q) = (6, 2); a 10-qubit variational circuit reached energy within 3.6% of exact, while 40-qubit MPS energy converged at bond dimension 768.
watch_item: Quantum advantage remains an estimate rather than a demonstration, and weak inter-dot entanglement can keep classical simulation tractable.
paper_title: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage
